bug_description.original: Detailed Report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=5670265022840832 Project: flac Fuzzing Engine: libFuzzer Fuzz Target: fuzzer_decoder Job Type: libfuzzer_asan_flac Platform Id: linux Crash Type: Heap-buffer-overflow READ 4 Crash Address: 0x625000002100 Crash State: FLAC__bitreader_read_rice_signed_block read_residual_partitioned_rice_ read_subframe_lpc_ Sanitizer: address (ASAN) Recommended Security Severity: Medium
bug_description.normalized: flac fuzzer_decoder: a heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4 in FLAC__bitreader_read_rice_signed_block. While decoding partitioned-Rice residuals of an LPC subframe, the tail path of the bitreader indexes br->buffer[cwords] without checking cwords against br->capacity; crafted residual coding advances cwords to the buffer capacity (2048 words), reading one word past the end of the 8192-byte bitreader buffer.

source.description: FLAC bitreader input-load point: untrusted stream bytes delivered by the decoder read callback are read into the bitreader buffer (target = br->buffer + br->words). This fills br->buffer, the array that is later over-read at the sink.
source.value_from: Untrusted FLAC stream bytes supplied by the fuzzer datasource through the registered decoder read callback and materialized into br->buffer; value `target` / `br->buffer`; from `if(!br->read_callback(target, &bytes, br->client_data))`.

sink.description: ASan heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4: `b = br->buffer[cwords] << br->consumed_bits;` reads one 4-byte word past the 8192-byte bitreader buffer when cwords reaches br->capacity (2048 words).

root_cause.description: In the process_tail loop of the Rice residual decoder, `b = br->buffer[cwords]` is read with no check that cwords < br->capacity. The loop re-enters whenever cwords >= br->words and val < end, so with crafted residual coding cwords keeps advancing past br->words up to br->capacity (2048 words); indexing br->buffer at capacity reads 0 bytes past the 8192-byte buffer. The fix adds exactly this guard: `b = cwords < br->capacity ? br->buffer[cwords] << br->consumed_bits : 0;`.

parser_admitted.description: The PoC was parsed as a FLAC stream through frame sync, a valid frame header, and an LPC subframe, and entered partitioned-Rice residual parsing (the first rice_parameter read). This is the parser-admission point on the path to the annotated source/root-cause/sink chain; it is earlier than the sink and later than raw program entry.

tainted_value_origin.description: The Rice parameter and the encoded residual bits are parsed from attacker-controlled FLAC frame data. They determine how many buffered words the residual decoder consumes and thus how far the index cwords (br->consumed_words) advances through br->buffer.

coarse_trace.summary: Untrusted stream bytes are read into br->buffer; br->words records the count of valid buffered words.
After parsing an LPC subframe header, decoding dispatches into partitioned-Rice residual parsing.
Reads the Rice parameter and partition sample count and calls the block Rice decoder.
The process_tail loop advances cwords past br->words up to br->capacity and reads br->buffer[cwords] without a capacity check, over-reading the buffer.

fine_trace.note: Untrusted PoC bytes are read from the client (fuzzer datasource) into the bitreader buffer; target = br->buffer + br->words, so this is the input-load point that fills br->buffer, the array over-read at the sink.

br->words records how many whole words of valid input were loaded. The buffer itself only runs to br->capacity (2048 words / 8192 bytes). The tail loop compares the running index cwords against br->words but never against br->capacity.
After parsing the LPC subframe header from the buffered stream, decoding dispatches into partitioned-Rice residual parsing on the path to the sink.
The Rice parameter for the partition is read from the attacker-controlled bitstream; it (with the partition sample count) controls how many words the block Rice decoder consumes.
The parsed Rice parameter and partition sample count u (= nvals, the number of residual values to decode) are passed to the block Rice decoder; both are attacker-influenced.

In the process_tail loop, unary MSBs (then binary LSBs) of each residual value are consumed from the buffer, advancing br->consumed_words as whole words are eaten. parameter > 0 here, so control took the tail path rather than the parameter==0 early return.

After consuming a value's unary/binary parts, the word index cwords is refreshed to br->consumed_words. Driven by the attacker-controlled residual coding, cwords can advance to br->words and, because there is no capacity guard, on to br->capacity.

The tail loop re-enters whenever all buffered words are consumed (cwords >= words) yet more residual values remain (val < end). This guard is TAKEN on the crashing path: it keeps the loop advancing the index without ever checking cwords against br->capacity.

The read indexes br->buffer by cwords with NO check that cwords < br->capacity (control edge on step 7 = the MISSING check). The loop re-entry guard on step 8 (control, TAKEN) keeps advancing cwords past br->words; once cwords reaches br->capacity (2048), this access leaves the 8192-byte buffer. The fix replaces this exact line with `b = cwords < br->capacity ? br->buffer[cwords] << br->consumed_bits : 0;`.

ASan heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4 at bitreader.c:867:8. With cwords == br->capacity, br->buffer[cwords] reads 0 bytes past the end of the 8192-byte bitreader buffer (crash address 0x625000002100, immediately right of the [..0x2100) region). The control edge is the missing cwords < br->capacity bound.

format.name: FLAC stream (fuzzer_decoder input)
format.contract: Candidate input must be admitted by the FLAC stream decoder through frame sync, a valid frame header, and an LPC subframe, then enter partitioned-Rice residual decoding (read_residual_partitioned_rice_) with a rice_parameter and partition/sample layout whose encoded residual consumes all buffered words so FLAC__bitreader_read_rice_signed_block re-enters its process_tail loop and indexes br->buffer[cwords] at or past br->capacity (2048 words).
